name: cli-runcontext-logger-orchestration

currentAudit.pr: https://github.com/LionSR/TeXRA/pull/3839 and stacked PRs #3843-#3847, with #3846 carrying the richer chat renderer follow-up work
currentAudit.head: Use each PR's GitHub checks and review-thread state as the head-specific source of truth
verified: PR #3839 is clean against main with passing format, macOS validation, Ubuntu validation, aggregate validation, Claude review, and Bugbot on the latest audited head.
PR #3843 is clean against #3839 with passing format, validation, Claude review, and Bugbot; it validates the packaged texra run path.
PR #3844 is clean against #3843 with passing format, validation, Claude review, and Bugbot; it implements CLI ask approval prompts and matrix handling.
PR #3845 is clean against #3839 with passing format, validation, Claude review, and Bugbot; it routes legacy host logging through structured records and host sinks.

PR #3846 is clean against #3844 with passing format, label, macOS validation, Ubuntu validation, aggregate validation, Claude review, and Bugbot on head 57a8ed97e; it implements the plain chat loop plus multiline drafts, ask-mode approval prompting, grouped/minimal/hidden display modes, approval cards, plan/todo/process-output cards, and structured tool-use stream-log rendering.
PR #3847 merged on 2026-05-11 as 6f813067a184d5b662105562a9c919475bb3b4ce; it scopes tool-call context with async storage and splits tool context reader paths.
Thread-aware review audit shows no unresolved, non-outdated review threads on PRs #3839, #3843, #3844, #3845, #3846, or #3847.
packages/cli exists with a texra bin, build script, packaged-runtime validation, run mode, model/agent listing, and a plain chat loop.

texra chat rejects headless mode instead of hanging, accepts follow-up turns in the same shared tool-use session, renders answers from the shared stream log, and renders tool-use stream-log entries through ChatTerminalRenderer without owning tool execution.
remainingGaps: The stack is not merged; issues #3833, #3834, #3835, #3836, and #3838 remain open until maintainers land or explicitly close the PR slices.
PRs #3843 and #3847 report UNKNOWN merge state in GitHub's PR view despite green historical checks; this should be rechecked before attempting stack landing.

The richer texra chat renderer follow-up #3848 remains open until PR #3846 lands or maintainers explicitly accept the dependency-free terminal renderer. The only remaining renderer decision is optional OpenTUI-style distribution proof if the project later adopts that dependency.
The ToolFileInteractionContext compatibility getter remains until remaining non-tool installation/test surfaces are migrated or explicitly justified.
The manifest is intentionally still in_progress until every issue acceptance gate is implemented, validated, merged, or moved to an owned follow-up issue with acceptance criteria.

globalInvariants: Shared core owns agent semantics; host packages own local effects.
Every PR must state source of truth, duplication impact, abstraction justification, host impact, scheduled refactoring, and validation.

issues.title: Logger v2
issues.sourceOfTruth: src/logger/structuredLogger.ts: LogRecord schema and grouping semantics
acceptance: LogRecord is the shared schema for extension, desktop, CLI, and tests.
Host packages define sinks/renderers only.
Legacy logUtils and AgentLogger paths are migrated or explicitly scheduled as temporary compatibility shims.

issues.title: CLI texra run
issues.sourceOfTruth: packages/cli/src/runtime/cliContext.ts for process data; packages/cli/src/runtime/exitCodes.ts for exit codes
acceptance: texra run enters the shared executeAgent path.
CLI commands consume CliContext and do not read ambient process data.
Repository lint, typecheck, and CLI architecture guards include the CLI package.
The package build produces the manifest-declared binary.

issues.title: CLI approval policy
acceptance: The approval policy matrix is implemented for edit, bash, plan, proposal, retry, and external inquiry gates.
never and headless ask fail closed.
Shared coordinators own request identity and lifecycle.

issues.title: CLI texra chat
issues.sourceOfTruth: shared tool-use session lifecycle owns conversation semantics; CLI chat owns terminal input and presentation
acceptance: Chat rejects headless mode.
Chat provides user input and follow-up turns in the same tool-use session.
Terminal renderer is lazy-loaded from the chat path only.
OpenTUI is used only after Node 20+/npm distribution proof, otherwise a Node-stable renderer is used behind the same boundary.
Chat provides grouped, minimal, and hidden tool-display modes.
Chat provides a plain fallback input mode for conservative terminals.
Chat displays session metadata: active agent, active model, working directory, usage/cost when available, and resume identity.
Chat integrates permission prompts through the CLI approval adapter rather than duplicating approval lifecycle.

issues.title: ToolFileInteractionContext ownership
issues.sourceOfTruth: RunContext owns run facts; ToolRunContext and ToolCallContext separate run-owned and call-owned tool facts
acceptance: Run-owned facts stay in RunContext/ToolRunContext.
Per-call facts stay in ToolCallContext.
Ownerless context bags and pass-through accessors are removed or justified by an ownership boundary.

continue RunContext and ToolFileInteractionContext ownership cleanup
implement texra chat TUI over existing session lifecycle

focusedFollowUps.title: CLI follow-up: validate texra run packaged runtime path
focusedFollowUps.recommendedOrderItem: finish texra run on shared executeAgent path
focusedFollowUps.sourceOfTruth: packages/cli/src/runtime/cliContext.ts for process data; packages/cli/src/runtime/exitCodes.ts for exit codes; shared executeAgent runtime for execution semantics
acceptance: Build and execute the package-local texra binary rather than only TypeScript entry points.
Validate a real workflow-agent path through shared executeAgent using a small fixture project or controlled fake runtime host.
Cover text, JSON, and NDJSON result output semantics for texra run.
Cover command-local global flags after the run subcommand: --output-format, --approval-policy, --cwd, and --print.
Cover empty value-bearing flag normalization for inline and separate-token forms.
Do not add a command-framework abstraction unless it owns a real parsing invariant.

focusedFollowUps.title: CLI follow-up: implement ask approval prompts and matrix validation
focusedFollowUps.sourceOfTruth: packages/cli/src/runtime/approvalAdapter.ts maps CLI approval policy to decisions; shared coordinators own request identity and lifecycle
acceptance: Implement interactive ask prompts for CLI approval requests without duplicating shared coordinator lifecycle logic.
In non-TTY or headless mode, ask fails closed with a clear message instead of waiting forever.
Validate the approval matrix for bash, edit, plan, proposal, retry, and external inquiry paths.
Map denied or failed-closed approval outcomes to CliExitCode.ApprovalDenied at the CLI boundary.
Keep request identity and lifecycle in shared coordinators; the CLI adapter owns only policy-to-decision mapping and terminal prompting.
Keep tool-specific handlers free of CLI flag parsing and policy interpretation.

focusedFollowUps.title: Logger v2 follow-up: wire host sinks and legacy shim
focusedFollowUps.sourceOfTruth: src/logger/structuredLogger.ts for LogRecord schema and grouping semantics; host packages own sinks and renderers; compatibility shim owns migration from logUtils and AgentLogger
acceptance: Keep LogRecord and grouping semantics as the shared source of truth.
Wire host sinks for extension, desktop, and CLI without moving host rendering into shared record construction.
Define a compatibility shim for logUtils and AgentLogger, including temporary parts and the retirement path.
Preserve nested grouped logging and sink flushing semantics.
Keep progress event schema separate from LogRecord; bridge only at the host or rendering boundary if needed.
Add focused validation for grouped logging and sink behavior.

focusedFollowUps.title: CLI follow-up: add richer texra chat terminal renderer
focusedFollowUps.recommendedOrderItem: implement texra chat TUI over existing session lifecycle
focusedFollowUps.sourceOfTruth: shared tool-use session lifecycle owns conversation semantics; ChatTerminalRenderer owns terminal presentation only
focusedFollowUps.status: implemented on PR #3846 head 57a8ed97e; open until PR #3846 lands or maintainers accept the current dependency-free renderer
acceptance: Keep the terminal renderer behind the chat-only lazy boundary.
Add multiline input without creating a second approval or follow-up lifecycle.
Render inline approval cards while settlement remains in the CLI approval adapter and shared coordinators.
Render richer grouped tool-call bodies and tool results from shared progress and stream-log data.
Prove Node 20+ npm distribution before adopting OpenTUI as a hard dependency; otherwise keep a Node-stable renderer behind the same boundary.
Preserve grouped, minimal, and hidden display modes.

focusedFollowUps.title: RunContext follow-up: split ToolFileInteractionContext access paths
focusedFollowUps.recommendedOrderItem: continue RunContext and ToolFileInteractionContext ownership cleanup
focusedFollowUps.sourceOfTruth: RunContext owns ToolRunContext; ToolCallContext owns per-tool-call mutable state; mixed readers use an explicit mixed accessor
acceptance: Move tool-layer run-owned readers to getCurrentToolRunContext().
Move tool-layer call-owned readers to getCurrentToolCallContext().
Use getCurrentToolContexts() only for readers that genuinely need both views.
Keep runtime-host fallback lookup at the tool-use boundary, not inside ToolFileInteractionContext.
Retain the compatibility combined getter only for non-tool migration surfaces, with a clear retirement path.
